title: Client Adaptor + Replayable Schema Guard for Usage Ingest
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We will add a lightweight client-side adaptor (sidecar pattern) and a replayable schema-guard pipeline to improve early detection of schema drift and reduce costly ingestion rejects downstream. The adaptor validates and tags events before they hit the primary ingest gateway, optionally buffering and forwarding a sampled replica stream to a replay service for offline analysis and fast rollback/rewrite.

Background / Problem:
- Production has seen a rise in schema-related rejections and silent truncations that only surface after downstream processing (billing, analytics) runs.
- Current server-side validators are necessary but cause noisy retries and operator load; drift detection happens late.
- We need a low-cost, incremental approach that reduces customer-impacting failures and accelerates root-cause for schema regressions.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Prevent a class of invalid events from reaching heavy processing paths by rejecting or sanitizing them at the edge client adaptor.
2) Provide a replayable, timestamped sample of pre-validated events to reproduce and diagnose schema regressions without affecting production throughput.
3) Maintain p95/p99 ingestion latency within current SLOs (p95 +2ms, p99 +8ms target for adaptor path).
4) Integrate signals into Console dashboards and alerting for schema drift and sampling-derived QA metrics.

Non-goals:
- This ticket is not a full replacement for server-side validation; server validators remain the source of truth for enforcement during rollout.

Scope & Features:
- Client adaptor (sidecar) shim that runs in customer SDK hosts and Console agents:
  * Performs schema lookup (local cache) and fast validation (type checks, required fields, top-level envelope shape).
  * Adds an X-Redwood-Schema-Version header when known.
  * Soft-reject mode and hard-reject mode configurable per deployment.
  * Local circular buffer for short-term replay (size configurable, default 2k events).
- Replay sampling service:
  * Receives a sampled replica stream from adaptors (1% default, configurable).
  * Stores indexable batches (by tenant, schema-version, timestamp) for 7 days in low-cost tier.
  * Provides a replay endpoint for PRs/QA and automated canaries.
- Schema registry cache:
  * Memcached-backed local cache with version TTL and async refresh from central schema service.
  * Fallback to server validation when cache miss occurs.
- Backpressure and flow control:
  * Adaptors observe ingest gateway headers (X-Ingest-Mode) to switch to best-effort batch or reduced sampling when downstream signals strain.
  * When server returns 429/503 annotated as backpressure, adaptors shift to sample-only mode and buffer locally with exponential backoff.
- Observability:
  * New metrics: client_validation_failures, client_sanitizations, replay_sample_rate, replay_storage_errors, adaptor_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), adaptor_buffer_fill_pct.
  * Dashboard cards & alert rules: schema-drift-rate > 0.5% sustained for 15m, replay_ingest_errors > 5/min.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Client-side validation reduces noise but increases SDK complexity and maintenance surface. We'll keep the adaptor as a thin process/library with small dependency footprint.
- Local buffer/replay avoids round-trip to central store for every event but introduces lost-replay risk on host crashes; acceptable if sampling remains small.
- Security: replay stream will be encrypted in transit and marked in audit logs; no PII enrichment performed during replay copy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Client adaptor returns schema decisions (accept/sanitize/reject) within latency targets and is configurable per-tenant.
- Replay service can accept and store sampled streams at the production scale of 2k events/sec aggregate during test window without data loss.
- Console dashboard surfaces a schema drift signal derived from adaptor+replay data and triggers the defined alert.
- A canary rollout plan exists and a PR with implementation (github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-adaptor PR#1234) passes load tests.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype adaptor library (Go) and sidecar binary; unit tests for validator logic.
2) Replay service prototype (Rust/Go) with S3-backed archival and 7-day index.
3) Integrate local schema-cache with central schema service endpoint.
4) E2E tests using synthetic drift scenarios and replay verification harness.
5) Canary rollout to internal tenants, then staged production.

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Microbenchmark adaptor CPU/latency with 95th/99th percentiles; target p99 adapter overhead under 8ms for common event sizes.
- Load test replay ingestion at 5x expected sample volume.
- Fuzz invalid envelopes to ensure sanitizers are safe and non-blocking.

Docs & Links:
- Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INGEST/pages/Client+Adaptor+Design (draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-adaptor/pull/1234 (prototype)
- Dashboard mock: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/schema-drift-mock

Migration & Rollout:
- Stage 0: Internal-only adaptor; sample-only + no hard rejects.
- Stage 1: Canaries for non-critical tenants (soft-reject enabled).
- Stage 2: Wider rollout with enterprise opt-out and hard-reject by policy.
- Rollback: adaptor can be remotely disabled via feature flag and will default to pass-through behavior.
comments: 2025-06-04 - Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff meeting notes added. Decided to keep client adaptor dependency-free as possible; prototype in Go. Confluence draft linked.
2025-06-07 - Jonah Mercado: Built initial validator logic and local cache; benching shows p95 +1.4ms, p99 +6.9ms on low-memory host. Next: replay proto and metrics plumbing.
2025-06-11 - SRE (Marcel Duarte): Reviewed backpressure plan. Requested explicit flow-control header agreement and added a requirement to annotate 503 responses with backpressure=true.
2025-06-14 - Product (Riley Chen): Requested that sampling rate be per-tenant and exposed in Console with override. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-06-18 - Jonah Mercado: Hooked up replay consumer to S3 test bucket and validated end-to-end for 50k sampled events. Two follow-ups: 1) add encryption-at-rest flag; 2) increase local buffer default to 5k for long-tail hosts.
